If for some $x \in R$, the frequency distribution of the marks obtained by $20$ students in a test is:
Marks 2 3 5 7
Frequency distribution ${\left(x + 1\right)}^{2}$ $\left(2x - 5\right)$ ${x}^{2} - 3x$ $x$
Then the mean of the marks is :
questions.explanation:
Total students $= 20 \implies {\left(x + 1\right)}^{2} + \left(2x - 5\right) + \left({x}^{2} - 3x\right) + x = 20 \implies {x}^{2} + 2x + 1 + 2x - 5 + {x}^{2} - 3x + x = 20 \implies 2{x}^{2} + 2x - 24 = 0 \implies {x}^{2} + x - 12 = 0 \implies x = - 4,3\left(∵x > 0\right) ∴x = 3$

Average $= \frac{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{2} \times 2 + \left(2x - 5\right)3 + 5\left({x}^{2} - 3x\right) + 7 \times x}{20} = \frac{32 + 3 + 0 + 21}{20} = 2.8$

Hence, required mean is $2.8$

Given,

${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}, \dots ..,{x}_{20}$ are in G.P with common difference $\frac{1}{2}$ and first term as $3$

Now using the formula for sum of G.P we get,

Now new sum of G.P with new data will be$= { \sum }_{i = 1}^{20}{\left({x}_{i} - i\right)}^{2} = { \sum }_{i = 1}^{20}{\left({x}_{i}\right)}^{2} + {\left(i\right)}^{2} - 2{x}_{i}i$

Now ${ \sum }_{i = 1}^{20}{\left({x}_{i}\right)}^{2} = \frac{9\left(1 - {\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)}^{20}\right)}{1 - \frac{1}{4}} = 12\left(1 - \frac{1}{{2}^{40}}\right)$

And ${ \sum }_{i = 1}^{20}{i}^{2} = \frac{1}{6} \times 20 \times 21 \times 41 = 2870$

And ${ \sum }_{i = 1}^{20}{x}_{i}i = 3 + 2.3\frac{1}{2} + 3.3\frac{1}{{2}^{2}} + 4.3\frac{1}{{2}^{3}} + \dots \dots .\mathrm{AGP} = 6\left(4 - \frac{11}{{2}^{18}}\right)$

So, mean of the new data will be,

$x = \frac{12 - \frac{12}{{2}^{40}} + 2870 - 6\left(4 - \frac{11}{{2}^{18}}\right)}{20} \implies x = \frac{2858}{20} + \left(\frac{ - 12}{{2}^{40}} + \frac{66}{{2}^{18}}\right) \times \frac{1}{20}$

Now $\implies \left(x\right) = \left(142.4 + 0.00001\right) = 142$

questions.question: Let sets $A$ and $B$ have $5$ elements each.
